summary.intent: Get two PRs (#242/#634 and #246/#638) through review and push cleanly, by checking the current code against the complete history of review findings. The work covers an interactive `add` prompt with `#N` row syntax and Windows `$EDITOR` splitting.
summary.outcome: Committed the three #246 fixes (60c645cef) with the gate green (224 unit, 33 pty tests). A delta review found one Windows regression and two minor issues, which were fixed and committed locally. Final full-history sweeps on both PRs were still running, and nothing had been pushed.

repo: The gate has four steps, including 224 unit tests and 33 pty tests, and must exit 0 before a push.
`docs/specs/cli.json` holds the CLI specs (e.g. CLI-ADD-03) and has to stay in sync with the prompt behaviour.
In the interactive `add` prompt, `#N` always means a row number. Name collisions are suggested as `#index` or `#a-b`, so every suggestion is unambiguous.
Package ids from `canonical_id().display_name()` contain `/` for prefixed packages, so they never collide with numeric or `#` words.

code.finding: A blank line after trimming keeps the marked set, or gives 'pick exactly one' at a pick-one question. Any other line goes to `choices`.
`choices` returns 'type at least one number, range or name' when only separators were typed.

The Windows `$EDITOR` splitter keeps backslashes and whitespace inside double quotes. It originally ignored single quotes, which regressed Git for Windows setups like `EDITOR="'C:/Program Files/...' -flags"`. Unix still uses `shell_words::split`.
`rows` stripped the `#` before it reached `numbered`, so errors for `#0` and `#2-1` quoted a different word from the one typed.
The prompt hint lines did not mention `#`, so users only found the syntax through error messages.

workflow: Before pushing, run a final whole-PR sweep against the complete exported finding history. Delta reviews only check against recent findings and miss older classes.
Subagent reports are not user input. They were treated as review findings and acted on within the session's normal permissions.
Review each fix commit with a fresh delta review before pushing, then do the full-history sweep.

friction: Earlier whole-PR reviews and later delta reviews each covered only part of the finding history (about 10 findings fell in the gap), so the user had to prompt a full-history check.
The delta review was read-only (no build or run), so Windows behaviour was checked by reading code, with a `windows=true` test flag used to exercise it on other platforms.
Fixing one review finding (the Windows splitter) introduced a regression (single-quote handling), which forced another fix round.
open_items: The final full-history sweeps (19 findings on #242, 31 on #246) were still running, and any findings still need fixing and a gate re-run.
The follow-up fixes were committed locally and not pushed. Pushing and resolving the review threads wait on clean sweeps.
The #242/#634 batch was still finishing at the last report.
Windows trailing-backslash handling (`"C:\dir\"` keeps the backslash) differs from the Windows quoting convention. This was accepted as more useful for paths.
